RFC 768 UDP Header: What is the purpose of the Source Port field (16 bits)?

What is the title/topic of <b>RFC 768</b: RFC 768 UDP Header: What is the purpose of the Destination Port field (16 bits)?
User Datagram Protocol: Target service port; watch for amplification services, unexpected high-value services, and scan fan-out.

What is the title/topic of <b>RFC 768</b: RFC 768 UDP Header: What is the purpose of the Length field (16 bits)?
User Datagram Protocol: UDP header plus payload length; mismatches or tiny/oversized lengths indicate malformed packets or evasion.

What is the title/topic of <b>RFC 768</b: RFC 768 UDP Header: What is the purpose of the Checksum field (16 bits)?
User Datagram Protocol: Integrity check over pseudo-header and payload; zero in IPv4 or invalid values can reveal crafted packets.

What is the title/topic of <b>RFC 768</b: RFC 791 IPv4 Header: What is the purpose of the Version field (4 bits)?
User Datagram Protocol: Should be 4 for IPv4; any other value indicates misclassification or malformed traffic.

What is the title/topic of <b>RFC 768</b: RFC 791 IPv4 Header: What is the purpose of the IHL field (4 bits)?
User Datagram Protocol: Header length; unusually large values imply IP options, while invalid short values are malformed.

What is the title/topic of <b>RFC 768</b: RFC 791 IPv4 Header: What is the purpose of the Type of Service field (8 bits)?
User Datagram Protocol: QoS/precedence byte; odd markings can indicate tunneling, policy abuse, or legacy stack artifacts.

What is the title/topic of <b>RFC 768</b: RFC 791 IPv4 Header: What is the purpose of the Total Length field (16 bits)?
User Datagram Protocol: Full packet length; mismatches with capture length can indicate truncation, evasion, or malformed packets.

What is the title/topic of <b>RFC 768</b: RFC 791 IPv4 Header: What is the purpose of the Identification field (16 bits)?
User Datagram Protocol: Fragment correlation value; predictable or repeated IDs help fingerprint hosts and spot fragmentation abuse.

What is the title/topic of <b>RFC 768</b: RFC 791 IPv4 Header: What is the purpose of the Flags field (3 bits)?
User Datagram Protocol: DF/MF fragmentation controls; watch illegal reserved-bit use and suspicious fragmentation patterns.

What is the title/topic of <b>RFC 768</b: RFC 791 IPv4 Header: What is the purpose of the Fragment Offset field (13 bits)?
User Datagram Protocol: Fragment position; tiny, overlapping, or excessive fragments are classic IDS evasion signals.

What is the title/topic of <b>RFC 768</b: RFC 791 IPv4 Header: What is the purpose of the TTL field (8 bits)?
User Datagram Protocol: Decrements each hop; unusually low or inconsistent TTL can indicate spoofing or traceroute probing.

What is the title/topic of <b>RFC 768</b: RFC 791 IPv4 Header: What is the purpose of the Protocol field (8 bits)?
User Datagram Protocol: Next-layer protocol number; unexpected values may indicate tunneling, scanning, or parser confusion.

What is the title/topic of <b>RFC 768</b: RFC 791 IPv4 Header: What is the purpose of the Header Checksum field (16 bits)?
User Datagram Protocol: IPv4 header integrity; invalid values suggest corruption, offload artifacts, or crafted packets.

What is the title/topic of <b>RFC 768</b: RFC 791 IPv4 Header: What is the purpose of the Source Address field (32 bits)?
User Datagram Protocol: Origin IPv4 address; private, bogon, or impossible sources on external links suggest spoofing.

What is the title/topic of <b>RFC 768</b: RFC 791 IPv4 Header: What is the purpose of the Destination Address field (32 bits)?
User Datagram Protocol: Target IPv4 address; unexpected internal, multicast, or broadcast destinations deserve review.

What is the title/topic of <b>RFC 768</b: RFC 791 IPv4 Header: What is the purpose of the Options/Padding field (32 bits)?
User Datagram Protocol: Optional and variable; rare on normal traffic, so source route/record route options are high-signal.

What is the title/topic of <b>RFC 768</b: RFC 793 TCP Header: What is the purpose of the Source Port field (16 bits)?
User Datagram Protocol: Client or service port; suspicious reuse, impossible services, or odd pairings can reveal scans or spoofing.

What is the title/topic of <b>RFC 768</b: RFC 793 TCP Header: What is the purpose of the Destination Port field (16 bits)?
User Datagram Protocol: Target service port; hunt for unauthorized services, fan-out scans, or policy bypass attempts.

What is the title/topic of <b>RFC 768</b: RFC 793 TCP Header: What is the purpose of the Sequence Number field (32 bits)?
User Datagram Protocol: Byte-stream position; repeated, predictable, or out-of-window values may indicate injection or spoofing.

What is the title/topic of <b>RFC 768</b: RFC 793 TCP Header: What is the purpose of the Acknowledgment Number field (32 bits)?
User Datagram Protocol: Next expected byte when ACK is set; impossible ACKs reveal scans, desync, or spoofed packets.

What is the title/topic of <b>RFC 768</b: RFC 793 TCP Header: What is the purpose of the Data Offset field (4 bits)?
User Datagram Protocol: TCP header length; large values mean options, while invalid small values are malformed.

What is the title/topic of <b>RFC 768</b: RFC 793 TCP Header: What is the purpose of the Reserved field (6 bits)?
User Datagram Protocol: Should be zero in RFC 793; non-zero reserved bits often indicate crafted or evasive traffic.

What is the title/topic of <b>RFC 768</b: RFC 793 TCP Header: What is the purpose of the TCP Flags field (6 bits)?
User Datagram Protocol: SYN/ACK/RST/FIN combinations; watch for illegal flag combos, SYN floods, or RST injection.

What is the title/topic of <b>RFC 768</b: RFC 793 TCP Header: What is the purpose of the Window field (16 bits)?
User Datagram Protocol: Advertised receive window; zero-window abuse, odd scaling, or fingerprintable values can stand out.

What is the title/topic of <b>RFC 768</b: RFC 793 TCP Header: What is the purpose of the Checksum field (16 bits)?
User Datagram Protocol: TCP integrity check; invalid values can be offload artifacts or crafted packet evidence.

What is the title/topic of <b>RFC 768</b: RFC 793 TCP Header: What is the purpose of the Urgent Pointer field (16 bits)?
User Datagram Protocol: Only meaningful with URG; unexpected use is rare and can indicate evasion or legacy attacks.

What is the title/topic of <b>RFC 768</b: RFC 793 TCP Header: What is the purpose of the Options/Padding field (32 bits)?
User Datagram Protocol: Variable options such as MSS, SACK, timestamps; odd combinations can fingerprint tools or evasions.

What is the title/topic of <b>RFC 768</b: RFC 1035 DNS Message Header: What is the purpose of the ID field (16 bits)?
User Datagram Protocol: Transaction identifier; repeated, predictable, or mismatched IDs can indicate spoofing or cache-poisoning attempts.

What is the title/topic of <b>RFC 768</b: RFC 1035 DNS Message Header: What is the purpose of the QR field (1 bits)?
User Datagram Protocol: Query/response bit; responses without queries or queries marked as responses are suspicious.

What is the title/topic of <b>RFC 768</b: RFC 1035 DNS Message Header: What is the purpose of the Opcode field (4 bits)?
User Datagram Protocol: Operation code; non-standard opcodes are rare and high-signal.

What is the title/topic of <b>RFC 768</b: RFC 1035 DNS Message Header: What is the purpose of the AA field (1 bits)?
User Datagram Protocol: Authoritative answer; unexpected authority can indicate spoofing or rogue infrastructure.

What is the title/topic of <b>RFC 768</b: RFC 1035 DNS Message Header: What is the purpose of the TC field (1 bits)?
User Datagram Protocol: Truncation flag; frequent truncation can force TCP fallback or indicate oversized abuse.

What is the title/topic of <b>RFC 768</b: RFC 1035 DNS Message Header: What is the purpose of the RD field (1 bits)?
User Datagram Protocol: Recursion desired; unexpected recursion from restricted networks can show resolver misuse.

What is the title/topic of <b>RFC 768</b: RFC 1035 DNS Message Header: What is the purpose of the RA field (1 bits)?
User Datagram Protocol: Recursion available; rogue or exposed recursive resolvers often reveal themselves here.

What is the title/topic of <b>RFC 768</b: RFC 1035 DNS Message Header: What is the purpose of the Z field (3 bits)?
User Datagram Protocol: Reserved bits; non-zero values are abnormal except negotiated extensions.

What is the title/topic of <b>RFC 768</b: RFC 1035 DNS Message Header: What is the purpose of the RCODE field (4 bits)?
User Datagram Protocol: Response code; spikes in NXDOMAIN, SERVFAIL, or REFUSED can reveal DGA, outages, or probing.

What is the title/topic of <b>RFC 768</b: RFC 1035 DNS Message Header: What is the purpose of the QDCOUNT field (16 bits)?
User Datagram Protocol: Question count; values other than one are uncommon and may be malformed or evasive.
